check.population: every extension point, plugin, registration and dependency construction site
check.freshness: a verdict stands until a plugin, a registration or the composition root changes
check.refusal: the dependency rule, plugin contract test or banned-API rule fails a change that hardcodes an extension or hides a dependency
check.observation: imports from the core to plugins, construction sites and registry contents, read from source and at startup
check.evidence: none: the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it
check.authority: the extension contract, which every plugin conforms to while the core names no plugin

records.name: Plugin Architecture
records.definition: A convention of building a small core that discovers and loads plugins through declared extension points.

records.name: Extension Points
records.definition: A mechanism that exposes named hooks or interfaces where new behavior can be added without editing the core.

records.name: Inversion of Control (IoC)
records.definition: A design rule that a framework or composition root owns object creation and control flow, and application code supplies the parts it calls.

distinctFrom.reason: Dependency injection supplies a dependency from outside, while an adapter makes an incompatible interface fit the one expected.
Dependency injection is passing dependencies in, while the composition root is the one place where they are wired.
Dependency injection is how one object receives its dependencies, while ports and adapters is how a whole core is isolated from its technologies.
Dependency injection passes a dependency in, while a singleton is reached through a global access point.

records.name: Dependency Injection
records.definition: A design pattern that passes an object its dependencies from outside, usually through its constructor.

distinctFrom.reason: A service registry resolves a key to a registered service, while health checks report whether an instance is ready to serve.

records.name: Service Registry
records.definition: A mechanism where services or plugins register under a key and are resolved by that key at runtime.

exemplar.before:
const fooService = new FooService(new SqlFooStore());
const barService = new BarService(new SqlBarStore());

distinctFrom.reason: A registry replaces a conditional over kinds with a keyed table, while a factory owns how one object and its defaults are built.

records.name: Registry Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern that replaces a conditional over kinds with a keyed table that each kind registers itself into.

records.name: Service Locator Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern in which code fetches its dependencies from a global registry at the point of use.
detected_by: service locator calls inside domain logic

records.name: Feature Toggle
records.definition: A mechanism that switches a code path on or off at runtime from externally held flag state, so a release can happen without a deploy.
detected_by: compile-time flags requiring redeploy to flip

exemplar.after:
if (featureFlags.enabled("new-foo-flow", { user, percentage: 10 })) runNewFooFlow();
else runOldFooFlow();
